newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 14.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Floods are now taking their toll on southern Moravia, but available reports say 32 people have died in northern Moravia and in the east of the Czech Republic. There is now a critical situation in Hodonin and Uherske Hradiste, and residents are being evacuated.

- According to the Governer of the Czech National Bank, Josef Tosovsky, if the crown were to weaken, the central bank would not prevent it from finding a new level to coincide with fundamental factors.

- On Friday, parliament approved the cabinet's request to take five billion crowns from revenue from small privatisations and to issue bonds worth another five billion crowns to cover damages in Moravia.

- While the increase in prices in construction for the first half of this year was 0.7 percent, prices of industrial products increased by 0.5 percent. Prices of initial materials increased only by 0.3 percent, but market services increased by 3.7 percent.
- From today, Moravia Banka is increasing its base rate to 16.50 percent and its prime rate to 19.90 percent.
- Expandia Finance estimates that GDP this year will increase at the most by one percent, because 25 to 42 percent of the Czech Republic's economic base took a blow from the floods in Moravia.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - President Vaclav Havel announced on Saturday that he will run for president again.
- The United States Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, arrived in Prague yesterday for a one-day visit, during which she will discuss Czech membership in NATO.

- Poldi Ocel, which went bankrupt in April, had a turnover last year of 779 million crowns and losses of 696 million. Poldi's debts of 3.2 billion crowns are irrecoverable, so its liabilities exceed its assets.

PRAVO - The investment company O.B. Invest, a member of the CSOB financial group, appealed against the Finance Ministry's decision to begin forced administration. The ministry said this was necessary to protect shareholders' interests.
- Some grocery retail franchises are reducing prices in flooded areas. For example, Pronto Plus decreased prices in Moravia by 10 to 20 percent.
- In a general meeting on Friday, shareholders of AGB IF 2 decided to decrease basic capital by 712.7 million crowns, which should go to create reserves for expected losses.
- The 32nd annual Karlovy Vary Film Festival ended on Sunday when the French-British film Ma Vie en Rouge, directed by Alain Berliner, won the Crystal Globe.

- According to Finance Minister Ivan Pilip, a programme is being prepared for support and renovation for industry and agriculture in areas affected by the floods. Pilip said damages cannot be estimated exactly, but they will be tens of billions of crowns and will have a long-term character.
LIDOVE NOVINY - According to Agriculture Minister Josef Lux, damages caused by floods in Moravia will not affect food prices. The Agriculture Ministry is considering imports with no customs charges.
- During the first quarter of this year, agricultural companies with more than 100 employees had total losses of 1.063 billion crowns, year-on-year 27 million crowns less.
- After surveying flooded areas in Moravia, experts from Skoda Plzen estimate losses at up to 100 billion crowns.
